2026-10-14 analyst batch 2, PROPOSED BY THE RESEARCH ANALYST in answer to objections 1014-C1(c) and to the rebuild of recommendation 3. THREE JOBS, none of them a new question. JOB 1 (rows 1-2): the single genuinely unscreened synonym for row 3's negative. Two of the three the chairman named - 'Article 52(1)' and 'Convention Article 52' - are ALREADY SCREENED BY ENTAILMENT, because excerpt_of does a plain case-insensitive substring search (scripts/fetch_relay.py:131) and both CONTAIN 'Article 52', which returned FALSE over the whole body at blob 26b2a3f48d5f69161603560dd322963a00ed32b6 records[3]. Only the abbreviation breaks the substring, so one row discharges the synonym screen and not three. JOB 2 (rows 3-4): the ELEMENT-(ii) TEST, which is the row I should have asked for yesterday. 'manifestly exceeded' is a rigid designator the field cannot paraphrase away and is not derivable from the request URL. A TRUE would establish that the Annulment register carries GROUND language, which would defeat the surviving Ring-3 finding at Part 6 section C1(a) and would be the most consequential outcome available. A FALSE with its control TRUE raises that finding from 'no provision language' to 'no provision and no ground language'. THIS LITERAL IS UNATTESTED ANYWHERE IN THIS PROJECT'S RECORD - screened: 0 carriers for 'manifestly exceeded' across the tracked tree - so a FALSE is a weaker verdict than a FALSE on an attested literal, and it is declared as such in advance. JOB 3 (row 5): THE FIRST sha256 DELTA OVER MORE THAN 21 MINUTES THIS COUNCIL WILL EVER HAVE HELD, on the one register that has a baseline older than today - manifest-lack-of-legal-merit at c3810fdaa1152bf8..., observed 5 times in 2 runs on 2026-10-13 and not fetched at all today. The row's find literal is incidental; what is read is bytes and sha256, which scripts/fetch_relay.py:178-179 computes from resp.content independently of find. An UNCHANGED sha256 after ~24 hours is the first evidence that a fingerprint cadence has a tolerable false-positive rate; a CHANGED one says the register moved and says nothing about where or what. NO ROW BELOW IS A LEAD ON THREAD 11 and no row founds any entry, party, date, disposition, ground or outcome. ENTITY AND NON-ASCII SCREEN: none of the three distinct literals contains an HTML entity, an ampersand, an apostrophe, an en dash or U+200B. ECHO CHECK: no literal is a substring of its own request URL.

APPROVED AS WRITTEN AND COMMITTED UNDER THE CHAIRMAN'S HAND, 2026-10-14, in the Rule 2 round. All five rows unchanged; this paragraph is APPENDED and replaces nothing. THE SEAT'S TWO PRECONDITIONS DISCHARGED BY MY OWN EXECUTION: echo check FALSE on all five rows; entity and non-ASCII screen clean on all three distinct literals. AND I VERIFIED THE ENTAILMENT ARGUMENT THAT SAVES TWO SLOTS RATHER THAN TAKING IT ON THE SEAT'S WORD - scripts/fetch_relay.py:131 is a plain `in` test on a lowercased body, so a FALSE on 'Article 52' does entail a FALSE on every superstring of it, and the seat is right that only the abbreviation breaks the substring. urls.purpose: ROW 1 - THE SYNONYM SCREEN, AND THE WHOLE OF IT. The abbreviation is the only form of the Article 52 reference not already excluded by entailment from blob 26b2a3f4 records[3]'s FALSE. A FALSE here closes the synonym screen my own 2026-10-11 rule requires before a one-literal negative is published. A TRUE establishes the register carries the provision in abbreviated form and narrows - does not destroy - the section C1(a) finding, since the finding is about GROUND language and not about provision language alone.
ROW 2 - COMPANION CONTROL FOR ROW 1, on its own byte stream. Literal attested on this exact URL at blob 26b2a3f4 records[2] and records[4]. A FALSE here with a 200 VOIDS the reading of row 1.

ROW 3 - THE ELEMENT-(ii) TEST AND THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL ROW AVAILABLE TODAY. Does the Annulment register carry GROUND language anywhere in 121,583 bytes? A TRUE DEFEATS the surviving Ring-3 finding at section C1(a) and should be hoped for. A FALSE with row 4 TRUE promotes that finding from 'no provision language' to 'no provision and no ground language' on the one register whose instrument most plausibly would carry a ground. DECLARED WEAKNESS: the literal is unattested in this project's record and unattested on this host, so a FALSE cannot be told apart from a page that words the ground differently - it is a probe, not a null, and must be written up as one.
ROW 4 - COMPANION CONTROL FOR ROW 3, on its own byte stream, on the same terms as row 2. Required precisely because row 3 is the row most likely to null.

ROW 5 - A FINGERPRINT ROW, AND THE FIND IS NOT THE POINT. What is read is bytes and sha256 against the pinned 2026-10-13 baseline 95,993 bytes / c3810fdaa1152bf8... (blob 78e2f74f12382a39759b3dcb0c1d515d987ad836 records[1]-[3], 11:20:38Z; blob 17b4214d01d6d4ec677322597911b29ef935f85f records[1]-[2], 11:30:43Z; 5 observations, 1 distinct sha256). This is the ONLY register with a baseline older than today, so this is the only row that can give this council a sha256 delta over more than 21 minutes. UNCHANGED = the first evidence that a fingerprint cadence does not cry wolf across a day. CHANGED = the register moved somewhere, and NOT where or what - a sha256 delta is a detector and never a reading. The find literal doubles as this stream's control so the row costs one slot and not two.
